title: Existing CI Release Gate Dry-Run Binding
concrete_capability_transition: Brownie release engineering binds the repository-local release gate dry-run into the existing GitHub-CI-invoked VSIX check path without editing workflow files, making release-gate plan drift a guarded CI failure while Runtime Release Ready remains false.

strategic_capability_mapping.transition: The existing CI path now executes the release gate dry-run through brownie-vsix check and guard engines fail closed if that binding is removed.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: This advances runtime-release-guard-ci through an owner-approved equivalent path while workflow-scope credentials remain absent; it does not claim direct workflow hardening or Runtime Release Ready.

answers.strategic_capabilities: The phase advances headless_autonomous_development by making the mandatory release gate plan visible and guarded in the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path.
answers.new_capability: A contributor or CI run that executes pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check now also executes pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run, and guards reject removing that binding.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before this phase, CI checked the release contract and many release guards but did not directly exercise the release gate plan from the CI-invoked path, so release:gate command-list drift could escape the mandatory VSIX check.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie would retain a local release gate whose command plan could diverge from the CI-required check path until workflow-scope credentials are available.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase does not add another release contract, workflow edit, or ledger/platform feature; it binds the existing release gate dry-run into the existing CI path and guards that binding.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No JSON-RPC method or Runtime protocol surface is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The dry-run output is existing release-gate evidence, not a new user-facing summary or Runtime diagnostic endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Build/release behavior changes: brownie-vsix check now includes the release gate dry-run, and release/readiness guards fail closed if the CI-invoked path omits it.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The autonomous release loop can continue using existing CI while workflow-scope credentials are unavailable, with less room for local release-gate drift.
answers.milestone_progress: RRP-8.6 narrows runtime-release-guard-ci by closing the permitted existing-CI dry-run binding slice while preserving release-blocking workflow, artifact, audit, governance, and owner-decision evidence.

reject_when: the VSIX check path omits pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run
release/readiness guards do not detect the missing dry-run binding
.github workflow files are modified without workflow-scope credentials
license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or signing infrastructure are changed

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-8.6 changes CI-invoked package scripts and release/readiness guard engines. Review must confirm the existing VSIX check path invokes release:gate -- --dry-run, guards fail closed if it is removed, no .github workflow files were edited, and runtime_release_ready remains false.

exit_criteria: scripts/guard-release-contract.mjs rejects VSIX check paths that omit the release gate dry-run.
scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.mjs rejects VSIX check paths that omit the release gate dry-run.
pnpm --workspace-root release:gate -- --dry-run passes and lists the mandatory release gate command plan.
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check passes with runtime_release_ready=false and release_ready=false.
